Melnytsya Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the old cemetery of Melnytsya, estimated to date to the 16th or 17th century alongside the local Jewish community's emergence, though Jews are recorded there as early as 1569; the population reached 1,599 (62 percent) by 1897. Per the town's own Yizkor memorial book, two Jewish cemeteries stood beside each other about 100 meters from the local beit-midrash; this older site had reached capacity and closed around 1908–09. During the interwar period, four synagogues, two libraries, a drama group, and an active heder operated; the population reached 875 by 1921. In early July 1941, following the German occupation, 60 Jews were murdered, with 280 more shot on July 16; by September 3, 1942, all of Melnytsya's Jews had been executed.
